trajectory.development: The Special Draw Right's review point falls in Book 24, where the labour gap is first met by people rather than a schedule and a generation that refuses to be counted is asked to give back the water before it is owed. The review tests the Right's training condition.
trajectory.becomes_available: The earlier condition: from Book 20 lineage crews carry channel repair under the Right (E1), and the Right is conditional on training outside apprentices (E7), so there is a condition for the review to test.
trajectory.changes: The lineage exemption stops reading as settled and becomes something to test. A generation that has never seen the labour (E6) is asked to take part, and the public capability record, separate from debt and tally, is first exported here (E5).

trajectory.development: Book 25 carries the maintenance lineages' stake in the review, which needs the condition demonstrated or the Right exposed, and the belief split across generations. Its excerpts repeat Book 24's element text (same source hashes), so no new development is visible here.
trajectory.becomes_available: Follows from the review point in Book 24 (s1) and the training condition (E7): the lineages have a stake only once the condition is in question. The stake is an agent inference in the record (E3, E9).
trajectory.changes: Reads the review as a contest over what counts as training and craft standard, not only over who holds the Right. This is inferred from E9, not a recorded position of the lineages.

trajectory.development: Apprentices from outside the lineage are trained under the Right's condition, so the labour starts to be shared craft rather than a lineage rota. This holds only if the review finds the condition met or the lineages accept the training as a standard.
trajectory.becomes_available: The training condition stated for the Special Draw Right (E7), once the review has put it to test (s1 and s2).
trajectory.changes: The rota is no longer carried only by lineage crews and households that can meet it (E1). A trained generation performs repair it has seen, which the record says it has not (E6), and the lineages' craft standards (E3) become something taught.

trajectory.development: A body or recognized practice gives the cohort standing in how the valley coordinates channel work, on the basis of practicing both counted and uncounted return. The record names no body and creates none (E8, hypothetical).
trajectory.becomes_available: The cohort's practice of both counted and uncounted return (E4, E8), available once outside apprentices have been trained (s3).
trajectory.changes: Labour moves from being performed to being coordinated: the question becomes who sets the rota and who may decide repair, not only who lifts. The uncounted practice in E4 becomes a claim rather than a gap.

trajectory.development: The public capability record exported in Book 24 is used to show who can repair rather than who owes, so capacity is seen across the households that carry the rota as well as the lineage crews.
trajectory.becomes_available: The record exists from Book 24 (E5); it can be used for coordination only once someone holds standing to use it (s4).
trajectory.changes: Repair becomes visible as capability, not only as obligation or tally, so families with few hands (E1) are seen for the repair they can do as well as the labour they are short of.

trajectory.development: Repair stops depending on a Special Draw Right held by lineage crews. The exemption closes as a special draw and remains as shared obligation carried through coordinated standing and the capability record. Earlier Books keep their own meanings, including the Books 9-11 repair skill (E1).
trajectory.becomes_available: Needs the cohort's standing (s4) and the capability record in use (s5), so that lineage crews are no longer the only labour the Right covers (E1).
trajectory.changes: Victory changes the world rather than restoring the start (E2): the labour is no longer a lineage privilege, while the lineage craft (E1, E3) remains, now shared.

relations.reason: The review can only test the Right's training condition if the Right exists as lineage-carried repair from Book 20 (E1) with that condition (E7).
The lineages' stake in the review exists only once the Right's condition is put to the test (E9, an agent inference in the record); E7 supplies the condition.
Fear of dilution by untrained gift-hands (E3) bears on the outside training that s3 requires (E7); the same craft standard can gate the training or teach it.
E8 bases the cohort's claim to standing on practicing both counted and uncounted return; in this proposed path that practice must come from training first (s3).
A record of who can repair (E5) helps coordination decide who does the work, though standing does not depend on it.
Training outsiders eases the household rota that falls on families with few hands (E1); both ask who carries the labour.
Closing the exemption needs standing for those who now perform repair. This dependence is proposed here and not stated in the record.

alternative_paths.ordering: Train outside apprentices before the Book 24 review, so the review tests a demonstrated condition rather than an exposed one.
alternative_paths.effect: The review becomes a confirmation rather than a threat, and the lineages' stake (E9) weakens because the condition is shown. The Right's exposure risk falls away, but the craft-standard dispute is not settled.

alternative_paths.ordering: Keep the Right unconditioned and let standing come from practice under the Right, without training outside apprentices.
alternative_paths.effect: The labour stays with lineage crews, and the uncounted generation gains standing from practice alone. The record states the Right is conditional on training, so this path changes the Right's terms.

alternative_paths.ordering: Let the capability record lead, before any body holds standing for coordination (s5 before s4).
alternative_paths.effect: Repair capacity becomes visible among households and crews while no one can act on it, so the rota may be recorded without being owned. The record names who can repair, but no body is created to assign work.

opportunities.text: The training condition (E7) and the Book 24 review together make it possible to show that repair can leave the lineage while the lineage keeps its craft; neither the condition nor the review shows this alone.
Counted and uncounted practice (E4), together with standing for those who practice both (E8), gives the uncounted generation a claim the count never gave them; the split alone does not.

The capability record (E5) and the Right's cost to families with few hands (E1) together let the rota be seen as capacity as well as load, so families who cannot meet it are recognized rather than only short.

reader_experience: Each Book should change what the labour means, not repeat who performs it. A reader meets repair first as an unseen duty under the Right, then as a condition under test, then as craft to be taught, then as a claim, and finally as shared capability. The channels and crafts keep their wonder, and the families who carry the rota keep their cost in view. As written, Book 25 restates Book 24, so repetition would be felt until its text develops.
open_decisions: Whether Book 25 keeps Book 24's element text (E9-E13 repeat E3-E7) or develops it.
Whether the Right's training condition is to be shown met or exposed at the review point (E7).
Whether a body or recognized practice is to grant the cohort standing in channel coordination (E8), and whether the author names one.
Whether the Special Draw Right closes as a special draw or stays as a standing exemption.
uncertainty: E2, E5 and E11 are truncated excerpts, and E14 lists all eleven citing elements as excerpted; the full Book 24 and 25 wording is not visible.
E7 says the source gives a reversal for the review point; the reversal is not in the excerpts, so the review outcome that s1 and s2 depend on is unknown.
E9-E13 share source hashes with E3-E7, so Book 25 restates Book 24. Whether this is intended carry-over or duplication is unresolved.
Lineage stakes and the cohort split are agent-proposed or derived attributions, and E8 is hypothetical; none is canon. Stage order follows dependency, not Book number.
